$comment: The reviewed inventory of every installed dependency whose license is not plainly permissive (VC-409).
check-dependency-licenses.mjs reads this file and fails when reality and this record disagree:
a new restricted dependency appears, a reviewed one changes version or relicenses, or a
containment rule that a review depended on stops holding.
Adding an entry here is a claim that someone READ the license. Do not add one to make CI green.
docs/licensing/dependency-license-review.md carries the reasoning and the open legal questions.
A key ending in `*` covers a family of per-platform packages. pnpm installs only the sibling
matching the current os/cpu, so `@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64` on a developer Mac is
`@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64` on CI. Three families need it; every other platform-specific
package in this tree is MIT or Apache-2.0.
Licenses that place no restriction on how Volli Code is used, shipped or charged for, beyond
attribution and warranty disclaimers. Attribution is still owed for these — that obligation
belongs to the centralized notice files, not to this gate.
A license is NOT listed here merely because it is common: copyleft (any GPL/LGPL/AGPL), the
weak-copyleft MPL, and every bespoke or unreadable license must be reviewed individually.

summary: Prebuilt libvips and its dependency stack, as one dylib. LGPLv3 applies to libvips itself and
to seven bundled components (fribidi, glib, libexif, libheif, librsvg, pango, proxy-libintl);
the rest of the table in the package README is permissive.
1.3.3 is what apps/desktop ships. 1.3.1 is build-time only: astro's own sharp@0.35.2 pulls it
into the store while building the website, and nothing in a distributed artifact loads it.
The package ships NO license text of its own — only the README's table of component licenses —
so the full LGPLv3 and GPLv3 texts LGPLv3 section 4(b) requires must come from elsewhere.
obligations: LGPLv3 4(a): prominent notice that the library is used and is covered by the LGPL.
LGPLv3 4(b): accompany the work with a copy of the GNU GPL and of the LGPL.
LGPLv3 4(c): name libvips among any copyright notices shown during execution.
LGPLv3 4(d): let the user relink the application against a modified libvips.
LGPLv3 4(e): Installation Information, where GPLv3 section 6 would require it.

$comment: The 4(d) half this gate can actually verify: the addon must reach libvips as a SEPARATE
shared library, so a user can substitute their own build of it. A statically linked libvips
would move us from 4(d)(1) to 4(d)(0)'s much heavier obligation without anything saying so.

summary: Bespoke license, not an SPDX one. It permits use only for predicting contrast for WEB content
on self-illuminated displays, prohibits commercial use without a signed agreement except under
the W3 cooperative agreement, forbids altering the algorithm's constants, and obliges a
licensee to track the latest non-breaking version.
Volli uses it in exactly one role: the independent oracle that packages/shared's own APCA math
is cross-checked against in tests, plus the desktop canvas-theming smoke. No source under any
src/ imports it, and nothing distributed contains it.
obligations: Stay development-only: the commercial-use prohibition and the AGPL fallback below only bite on
distribution or commercial use.
Keep current: the range must stay a caret range so the latest non-breaking 0.1.x is installable.

summary: apca-w3's only runtime dependency, and the sharpest license in the tree: AGPL v3, whose
source-offer obligation is triggered by conveying the work OR by letting users interact with
it over a network.
Neither happens. It arrives transitively under a devDependency, and the containment rule below
is what keeps it that way — this is the entry that makes apca-w3's dev-only status load-bearing
rather than merely true today.
obligations: Never becomes a direct dependency and never enters a distributed artifact.

summary: GreenSock Standard License (Webflow), effective 2025-04-30, read at gsap.com/standard-license.
Permitted Uses cover any website, web application or digital interface, commercial included and
at no charge. The one restriction that could reach Volli is Prohibited Uses: GSAP may not be
used in tools that let users build visual animations WITHOUT CODE in a way that competes with
Webflow's visual animation building. The licensor's own FAQ places AI code-generation tools
outside that prohibition.
Section III.3 additionally forbids removing GSAP's proprietary notices — which the production
website build was doing until this ticket; see apps/website/scripts/check-bundled-license-notices.mjs.
obligations: Keep the /*! legal banners in the deployed bundles (III.3).
Stay out of the desktop product, where the no-code-animation-builder question would arise.
Re-read the terms on a version bump: section VI.2 lets Webflow revise them, and using a version
released after a revision is what accepts it.

summary: Tailwind's CSS transformer, and astro's, plus its per-platform native binary. Weak copyleft at
FILE level: the reciprocity obligation attaches to modified MPL-covered files, and we modify
none — it is consumed as a published package and runs only while building.
No MPL-covered code reaches a distributed artifact; what ships is the CSS it emitted, which is
our own content.
obligations: Do not fork or patch it without taking on MPL 2.0 section 3.2 source availability.
Attribution in the notice files, as for any dependency.

summary: Dual-licensed, so the choice is ours. Volli elects Apache-2.0, which is already the dominant
license in this tree and carries no reciprocity. Recorded because the elected half must appear
in the notices — an entry reading only "MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0" leaves the reader guessing.
obligations: Notices must state Apache-2.0 as the elected license.

summary: Dual-licensed; Volli elects BSD-3-Clause, so the GPL-2.0 half is never exercised. Reaches the
store under @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime and electron-builder's signing tooling.
obligations: Notices must state BSD-3-Clause as the elected license.

summary: Dual-licensed; Volli elects BSD-3-Clause.
obligations: Notices must state BSD-3-Clause as the elected license.

summary: No `license` field in its manifest, so automated scans report it as unknown. Its `license` file
is the plain MIT text, copyright 2019-present Fabio Spampinato and Andrew Maney. Arrives under
mermaid, which the desktop renderer bundles.
obligations: MIT attribution, from the license file rather than the manifest.

summary: A generated napi platform package with no `license` field and no license file — the shape most
native-binding sub-packages ship in. Its parent `yuku-codegen@0.5.48` declares MIT, and the
binding is published from the same repository (yuku-toolchain/yuku) in the same release.
obligations: MIT attribution, inherited from the parent package.

summary: As @yuku-codegen/binding-*; parent `yuku-parser@0.5.48` declares MIT.
obligations: MIT attribution, inherited from the parent package.
